basis: Predicted CLI 82 (simulated mean 82.34, mode 82 at 33%, then 83 at 30%, 81 at 18%). Bucket 82-83 comes out 62.2% against a 54c ask (fee 2c, breakeven 56%), EV about +6c/unit. Chain: Open-Meteo curve_max 81.0, plus the measured curve bias +0.25 (metar_max minus curve_max, n=11 completed days, resid sd 0.84) = METAR max 81.3; round; plus the empirical DEN CLI offset {0:7, 1:16, 2:10}, mean +1.09, n=33, never negative. DECISIVE CHECK MADE TODAY: corr(morning curve_dev, final metar_max - curve_max) = -0.009 over 11 completed days, regression slope -0.003. The morning deviation carries NO information about where the day lands against curve -- sample mean morning dev is +0.92 while the mean final error is only +0.25, i.e. mean reversion, matching the known KDEN result corr(11:53 temp, remaining rise) = -0.635. So today's -1.4F deficit at 08:53 MDT is deliberately IGNORED rather than subtracted. Model family is tight and supports the curve: om_best/GFS 81.0-81.2, ICON 79.9, MET-No 82.0; NWS grid 85 excluded as the lone outlier. Conditions favour efficient heating: dewpoint 38F, soil moisture 0.141 m3/m3, FEW 8000/22000 (cirrus, non-capping), PoP 0.
caveats: Resid sd 0.84 is fitted on n=11 with two parameters and is probably optimistic; most of the distribution's width is the CLI offset draw rather than forecast error, so this call implicitly claims the meteorology is near-settled off eleven days. The zero-correlation check is an ad-hoc look made today, not a registered test -- it excluded the live day but is still an unregistered slice. I had discounted DEN toward 80-81 three times earlier in the same session on that -1.4 deficit and RETRACTED it when the correlation came back zero; this call is the corrected version, so the reasoning moved within one session.
